title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
key_facts: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded; it was the lowest quarter of the year so far but above every quarter since Q2 2022.
That is down 25% from $212 billion in Q2 and up 53% from $104 billion in Q3 2025; $679 billion was raised in the first three quarters, the highest for that period in any year.
A record 27 companies raised rounds of $1 billion or more (16 in Q2, 14 in Q1); around a third of Q3 funding went to them.
Eight companies raised $3 billion or more, with frontier labs and data centers leading; the largest rounds, $5 billion each, went to Databricks and Safe Superintelligence.
AI-driven startups raised $102 billion, 64% of the total, down from the two previous quarters but 14 percentage points above Q3 2025.
US-based companies raised $91 billion, about 57% of the total; the San Francisco Bay Area alone took 24%.
Data are as of 2 Oct 2026 and lag most at the earliest stages, so seed totals tend to rise after a quarter ends; the figures are based on reported data.
quote_evidence: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows.
An all-time record of 27 companies raised such sizable rounds in Q3 2026, an increase from the previous record, set in Q2, of 16 companies and Q1’s total of 14 companies.
Note that data lags are most pronounced at the earliest stages of venture activity, with seed funding amounts increasing significantly after the end of a quarter/year.
why_it_matters_hint: A third of the quarter's venture money went to just 27 companies, mostly AI labs and data-centre builders.
event_date: Crunchbase report published 5 Oct 2026, covering July to September 2026 (data as of 2 Oct 2026)
notes: Full Crunchbase article read. It is Crunchbase's own data analysis (one outlet); deal details it mentions (for example Nvidia and Hugging Face) were not checked elsewhere and are not used. Figures are in US dollars.
